einstellungen.text: You have to give up your mom's garden. By six in the morning.
Your mom is sitting under the crooked tree. Her hand rests on the bark.
Your space station only repairs itself with empty rooms. Five failures. One big room.
It smells like damp earth. The leaves rustle in the air vents.
The heavy beds won't fit anywhere. Not in the halls. Not in the dome.
Ren shows up with empty trays.
"A garden fits in your hand too."
You fill two hundred little packets with seeds. Tomatoes, beans, cress.
Plus sixty-four seedlings. Bo carries his little bowl like it's made of glass.
Your mom measures the tree. Eight feet. She writes the number on the wall.
Nobody can carry the tree. She leaves it standing.
You carry everything into the dome. Where the planet glows through the glass.
On the way back, your mom carries Bo's bowl. She smiles for the first time in days.
Ren digs out the last bed. Then he stops.
Under the soil lies an old blueprint. Your living ring should have been replaced long ago.
